definitions.explanation: The sacred text of Christianity, comprising the Old and New Testaments. In Japanese, this word specifically refers to the Christian Bible.

examples.japanese: {聖書|せいしょ}を{読|よ}むのが{日課|にっか}だ。
examples.english: Reading the Bible is my daily routine.

examples.japanese: ホテルの{部屋|へや}に{聖書|せいしょ}が{置|お}いてあった。
examples.english: There was a Bible placed in the hotel room.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}には{聖書|せいしょ}からの{引用|いんよう}がたくさん{含|ふく}まれている。
examples.english: This novel contains many quotations from the Bible.

notes:
USAGE:
Refers specifically to the Christian Bible. The word is also used figuratively to mean an authoritative or definitive reference in a field (e.g., 「この{本|ほん}はプログラミングの{聖書|せいしょ}だ」 — "This book is the bible of programming").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {聖書|せいしょ}を{読|よ}む (read the Bible)
- {旧約聖書|きゅうやくせいしょ} (Old Testament)
- {新約聖書|しんやくせいしょ} (New Testament)
- {聖書|せいしょ}の{教|おし}え (teachings of the Bible)

NOTE:
Do not confuse with the homophone {清書|せいしょ} (fair copy — making a clean, final copy of a document).

cross_references.notes: Same reading but different meaning: fair copy, clean copy
